motion.why: 2026-11-05 (Mike: move as the motors really can, generous S-shaped speed-up / slow-down so nothing wobbles or skips). Joint output speeds deg/s and accelerations deg/s^2. A NEMA 17 keeps ~0.40 N.m at ~300 rpm (24 V, 2 A) = 48.6 deg/s through the 37:1 drive; loaded joints run well under that. Swivel: 4:1 bevel, limited by the arm's inertia (wobble), not torque. | 2026-11-05 (Mike: push the cruise rpm): tools/motor_speed.py - pull-out torque at 24 V vs the worst gravity load anywhere on the board, x1.5 margin, printed-cycloid input capped at 600 rpm until bench-tested: J2 80 deg/s (493 rpm), J3 / J4 95 (586 rpm), J1 45 (277 rpm: its margin at full reach is only x1.13 at ANY speed and the 60 mm motor's coil figures are estimated), swivel 90 (60 rpm at the motor; its ramps, not the motor, limit it). Accelerations unchanged. Measured on the seed-5 game: cruise alone buys ~0.1 min - the moves are short and J1's acceleration sets the pace.

dynamics.why: 2026-11-07 Mike: 'speed up the acceleration ... takes forever to get up to speed'. tools/motor_speed.py --write. The viewer's planner times each move with the arm's own dynamics along its path: every joint's torque = sum of m (a - g) . dp/dq over the masses below (+ rotor J R^2 eff q''), kept under pullout x ratio x eff / margin at every sample of the move; a joint's acceleration is never held below its scalar a (today's) nor above a_cap (motor rev/s^2 cap). Masses kg: links as two points (their own m L^2/12), drives at the joints, claw half way down the tool, a king at the grip.
dynamics.bodies_why: 2026-11-22 tools/arm_mass.py --write: every solid of the chain-drive arm at its own centre (main's parts + the chaindrive studio's screws, nuts, pulleys and chains; covers and cables ESTIMATED), one body per moving group in its link's frame. Replaces masses.link / drive / wrist_drive / claw where present; masses.king stays. 2026-11-23: J4 is the herringbone planetary (459 g as printed, was the cycloid's 597): housing with link C, carrier side with the claw.

motion.why_chain: 2026-11-22 (Mike: 'the correct expected accel and decel we can get out of that at speeds'): the chain-drive arm, tools/arm_mass.py --write then tools/motor_speed.py --write. Every part weighed (5.7 kg beyond the shoulder + a king); J1 74.6:1 (SFU1204 + 32T:60T), J2 / J3 39.8:1 (60T:60T), swivel 27:1; efficiency 0.82 ESTIMATED. 2026-11-23: J4 the herringbone planetary, 5.25:1 at ~0.91 (was the 37:1 cycloid at 0.65), the arm 5.5 kg. Each joint's cruise is the motor rpm that makes a typical move quickest while the WORST chess pose keeps x1.5 over gravity + inertia + what the motor spins; a = that pose's limit (= deceleration), capped at 40 rev/s^2 at the motor. Elbow at x1.3 (x1.5 now holds with the lighter wrist but leaves only 68 deg/s^2: Mike's call); swivel held at 110 deg/s^2 (wobble) though its torque allows ~460.

park.why: 2026-11-09 Mike: tool-changer dock (park_dock.py). Grip points (design) for the moves; 'pose' = the parked joint angles (the IK's own there: J4 level with J1, J2 = J3), which the arm assumes at power-up.

keep_out.note: the fork, post and foot: no claw below 'below_up' (mm above the board) with J0 in this range except the park moves themselves

startup.why: 2026-11-09 Mike: "check if it's sitting in the dock before we try to home it out" - the dock's Hall (DRV5032FB in the fork's lug) sees the 6x2 magnet in the claw's ring only when the claw is seated.
power_up: read the dock Hall (several reads, as homing does: 5 Hz sensor)

MADE = parked: take 'pose' as the joint angles and run the plain home cycle (J1..J4, then J0) - no special moves (Mike 2026-11-09: 'just running a regular home cycle when the arm tilts back, it's going to clear the dock'). Measured 2026-11-24 with the station 18 further out (dock_homing_check.py; J1 at 0.1 deg to +6, then 1 deg to its overshoot): nothing touches the station; closest 0.26 mm at J1 +0.5 deg as the claw flange rises past the pocket wall, 1.3 mm by +1 deg, then >= 5.3 mm (the claw hub at +11 deg) and 39 mm by +39; the J2, J3, J4, J0 stages and the move to home stay >= 27 mm off (2026-11-10, at the old place: 0.24 mm at +0.6 deg)

CLEAR = not in the dock: the angles are unknown, so no park moves and no blind homing; motors off, say so on the screen, wait for the player (push it into the dock by hand, or choose home-from-here) - to settle with Mike
startup.parking: after over -> outside -> lifted -> seat, the dock Hall must read MADE before the arm is called parked (the parked flag is set) and the motors let go; CLEAR there = a missed seat: stop, report

park.moved: 2026-11-24: grip point 18 further out (reach 197.5, was 179.5) - the station moved straight out to clear the new chain swivel's base, cover and yoke (park_dock.py RHO)

bowden.why_2026_11_21: Robot arm control and kinematics, 2026-11-21 (bowden_route.py; Mike: 'I want that tube moved and internal wire' - the old route ran through the chain arm's motors and didn't start at the servo's fitting). The tube leaves the yoke's servo-shelf fitting straight back, loops up behind the shoulder through a ring on a post, and runs down the arm's -Y side at z ~100 through rings reaching over each knuckle, past link C's motor, then in to the claw. Measured against the real parts over every square and tray spot (0/10/60/125 up): tightest bend r 31.6 (PTFE min 30) and >= 14.8 mm clear of everything while the wrist is <= 100 deg (9.5 at 110, 4 at 120). With the wrist past ~130 (the squares next to the robot) the last ~100 mm into the claw crosses link C's unfinished free end - the claw itself overlaps it there too: settled when the wrist (J4) drive is designed.

homing.why: 2026-11-05 Mike: the Home button runs a CNC-style homing cycle. tools/hall_homing.py: each switch's Hall point and magnet carry a sphere, radius trip/2 - touching = the Hall is made (trip = the distance at which a DRV5032FB, ~4.8 mT, switches over a 6 x 2 magnet). Joints without a switch yet go straight to their home angle first; then each switch: seek (dir) at seek deg/s until it reads made, back off at back (back_slow from just before first contact) until it reads clear + pull_off deg, in again at back_slow and creep back on at creep: where it reads made is home. The Hall reads the field sample_hz times a second, so it reports up to 1/sample_hz late. Then the arm goes to its home pose. Switches home in list order: shoulder, elbow, J3, wrist, then the turntable.
